findings.explanation: The title presents this as an ASHRAE exceedance, but the ASHRAE TC 9.9 recommended envelope (A1–A4) is −9°C dew point to 15°C dew point and 60–70% RH max, and A1 allowable is 8–80% RH; 40% RH is an obsolete pre-2008 lower limit. Readings of 30–40% RH are within ASHRAE guidance yet would be reported as ASHRAE exceedances.
findings.quote: Use sliding windows to alert only if out of 40–60% RH for >15 minutes.
findings.suggested_fix: Base the low limit on dew point (−9°C DP) and the high limit on 15°C DP plus 60% RH (or 70%/50% RH per the 2021 pollution note), or keep 40–60% RH but describe it as a site policy band rather than ASHRAE. The grounding guide's '8-80% RH' is the A1 allowable range, not the recommended one.

findings.explanation: The Universal Forwarder is a separately downloaded Splunk binary, not a Splunkbase app (splunkbase.splunk.com/app/617 returns 404), and it has no bundled Python for SNMP modular inputs.
findings.quote: Collected via Universal Forwarder (Splunkbase 617) modular input or scripted poll into the index named in the SPL.
findings.suggested_fix: Name Splunk Connect for SNMP (Splunkbase 6266) or the SNMP Modular Input (Splunkbase 1537) on a heavy forwarder, and list the fields the SPL needs: zone, humidity_pct (and dew point / temperature if the ASHRAE logic is adopted).

findings.explanation: implementation requires an excursion lasting more than 15 minutes, detailedImplementation says the UC targets short excursions, and the SPL does neither: it counts individual out-of-band samples per zone with no duration logic; visualization promises 'max excursion minutes', which the SPL never computes.
findings.quote: Stricter alerting for short excursions supports tape media and corrosion-sensitive gear beyond static high/low limits.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one intent (sustained >15-minute excursion is the common choice), describe how duration is measured (e.g. consecutive samples or streamstats over time), and remove the contradicting sentence.

findings.explanation: The scenarios are generic and name no real cause of misleading humidity readings.
findings.quote: **Synthetic probe on `zone`, `duration_bucket`** — Health checks in `environment` populate the same fields the SPL groups on.
findings.suggested_fix: List real causes: humidifier/dehumidifier cycling or CRAC fighting, outside-air economizer mode on dry or humid days, sensor drift or uncalibrated probes, sensors placed in hot aisles where RH reads low, and door-open events.

findings.explanation: A 300–900 s poll cannot support a >15-minute persistence rule reliably (one to three samples), and 'earliest=-24h@h' counts the whole day; Steps 1–4 are duplicated with 'Step 4 — Operationalize' repeated four times.
findings.quote: Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower.
findings.suggested_fix: Poll every 60 s, schedule the search every 5–15 minutes over a short window, and deduplicate the steps.

findings.explanation: The UC uses polled humidity values, not traps.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the polled SNMP environmental sensor model instead of snmp_trap.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: '(ASHRAE)' asserts that 40–60% RH is the ASHRAE threshold; current ASHRAE TC 9.9 humidity limits are dew-point based with no 40% RH floor (see ASHRAE 2021 reference card). Either change the thresholds or drop ASHRAE from the title.

`duration_bucket` holds only 'high'/'low' and measures no duration; `stats count by zone, duration_bucket` counts samples, so a single sample out of band alerts, contradicting the >15-minute rule. The 40% floor is not ASHRAE-based.

summary: The UC labels a 40–60% RH band as an ASHRAE threshold although current ASHRAE TC 9.9 guidance defines humidity by dew point and has no 40% RH floor; the promised 15-minute persistence is not implemented, and the collection path names a non-existent Splunkbase Universal Forwarder app.
